faq.q: Can I swim in the sea in Marbella in November?
faq.a: Yes, but it’s brisk. The average sea temperature is 18°C, so a wetsuit or a quick dip is fine. Most charters include towels and warm showers onboard. If you’re sensitive to cold, stick to midday when the sun is highest.

faq.q: What’s the wind like in Marbella in November?
faq.a: Typically light Levante winds at 5-10 knots, making for calm seas. Stronger Poniente winds are rare but can bring a few choppy hours. Your skipper will choose a sheltered route along the coast if needed.

faq.q: Do I need a jacket on a boat in November?
faq.a: A light jacket or fleece is recommended for early morning or sunset cruises. During midday, a long-sleeve shirt is enough. All our boats have indoor saloons with heating – the Azimut 58 Flybridge is particularly cosy.

faq.q: Is November a good month for dolphin watching?
faq.a: Yes, November is excellent. Pilot whales and common dolphins are frequently spotted off the Marbella coast. The quieter seas and lower boat traffic make sightings more likely. Bring binoculars.

faq.q: Which boat is best for November weather?
faq.a: The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) has a heated indoor saloon and panoramic windows – perfect for cooler days. For a smaller group, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) offers a covered cockpit and good value.

faq.q: How many hours of sunlight do I get in November?
faq.a: Sunrise is around 7:45 AM, sunset about 6:15 PM – roughly 10.5 hours of daylight, with about 6 hours of direct sun. Plan your charter between 10 AM and 4 PM for the best light.

faq.q: Are there any festivals or events in Marbella in November?
faq.a: The Marbella Film Festival usually takes place in November, along with the San Juan de Dios fair. The town is quieter than summer, so you’ll find easier restaurant bookings and less crowded beaches.

faq.q: What should I pack for a November boat charter?
faq.a: Sunscreen (UV is still strong), a light jacket, sunglasses, a hat, and a swimsuit if you plan to dip. Non-slip shoes are wise. Your skipper provides towels, drinks, and snacks – just bring your camera.

data.body_html:
Thinking about a Marbella boat rental weather November 2027? The numbers are better than you think: average sea temperature of 18°C, 6 hours of daily sunshine, and light Levante winds that keep the sea calm. While summer crowds have vanished, the Costa del Sol still delivers mild days perfect for a relaxed charter. Here’s what the real forecast looks like – and which boats suit the season best.

November 2027 Weather Averages for Marbella

Based on long-term climate data, November in Marbella sees:

  • Air temperature: 16°C to 20°C (61-68°F) – warmest around 2 PM.
  • Sea temperature: 18°C (64°F) – swimmable with a wetsuit or quick dip.
  • Sunshine: ~6 hours per day – UV index still 3-4, so wear sunscreen.
  • Rain: only 4-5 rainy days, usually short showers.
  • Wind: light Levante at 5-10 knots – calm seas, rarely above Force 3.
  • Water clarity: excellent – visibility up to 20 metres in calm conditions.

These conditions make November one of the best-kept secrets for a Marbella boat rental – no queues at Puerto Banús, easier mooring, and lower prices.

Why November Is Ideal for a Boat Charter

Most visitors think summer is the only season for boating, but November offers distinct advantages:

  • No crowds: Puerto Banús is quiet – you’ll find a berth easily and enjoy the marina without the summer bustle.
  • Better wildlife sightings: Pilot whales and common dolphins are more common in November, often spotted between Marbella and Estepona.
  • Pleasant temperatures: 18-20°C is ideal for lounging on deck without overheating.
  • Lower rates: Many Tier A boats like the Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) are available at peak-season prices but with more flexibility.

Pack a light jacket for the morning, and you’ll enjoy a comfortable day on the water.

Best Boats for November Conditions

For cooler mornings, a boat with a heated indoor saloon is a game-changer. Our top picks:

What to Expect from Your Skipper in November

Our licensed skippers are experienced with late-season conditions. They’ll:

  • Choose sheltered routes – e.g., from Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro or Cabopino.
  • Adjust speed and course based on wind and swell.
  • Provide blankets and hot drinks on request.
  • Recommend the best time of day (usually 11 AM – 4 PM for warmth).

All charters include fuel, insurance, and Spanish IVA – no hidden costs.

November Itinerary Suggestions

With shorter daylight, a half-day charter (4-6 hours) is ideal. Consider:

  • Puerto Banús to Cabopino: 1.5 NM east – sheltered coves, calm waters, and a beachside lunch stop.
  • Puerto Banús to Estepona: 12 NM west – scenic cliffs, dolphin hotspots, and the charming Estepona marina.
  • Marbella coastline cruise: Pass the Golden Mile, La Concha mountain backdrop, and stop for a swim at Cala Cortés.

Your skipper will tailor the route based on the day’s weather.

What’s Included in Your Charter

Every booking comes with:

  • Licensed English-speaking skipper
  • Fuel and all mooring fees
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava
  • Light snacks (e.g., olives, crisps, nuts)
  • Towels, snorkel gear, and safety equipment
  • 21% Spanish VAT

No surprises – just show up and enjoy.

Book Your November 2027 Charter

Ready to experience Marbella from the water in November? Browse our full fleet or contact us via WhatsApp for pricing on specific boats. The Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are available from €749 for 2 hours – a perfect short escape. For a full-day adventure, the Mangusta 80 (from €4,719 for 4 hours) includes a free jet ski.

Don’t wait – November slots fill quickly with savvy travellers who know the value of a quiet, sunny charter.
